questions.explanation: Bandwidth names the raw transmission capacity of a link, so it is a rate. Propagation delay is the time a bit needs to travel across the medium, and goodput is the rate of useful data that actually arrives after overhead, retries and congestion are accounted for. Conflating these quantities leads to wrong capacity plans because a fast link with long delay can still underperform. The concrete addresses in the case do not change the rule.
